vulnerabilities.description: Due to the design of the name constraint checking algorithm, the processing time of some inputs scale non-linearly with respect to the size of the certificate. This affects programs which validate arbitrary certificate chains.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not validate arbitrary certificate chains in its lpm runtime path.

ratings.justification: The only runtime use of lpm is an outbound download helper. It does not accept attacker-controlled certificate chains or custom PEM inputs, so the x509 name-constraint path is not exercised.

analysis.detail: Go stdlib crypto/x509 name-constraint vulnerability. NVD fixes the 1.25 line in Go 1.25.3 and the 1.24 line in Go 1.24.9; the scanner reported go1.25.1 for this image. Liquibase Secure only installs lpm 0.3.6 from a release ZIP (docker/Dockerfile:39-55), and the entrypoint only invokes it when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4-5). Repo-wide source greps found no crypto/x509, SystemCertPool, or CertPool usage in application code, so the arbitrary certificate-chain path described by the advisory is not exercised.

CVE-2026-39821 / GO-2026-5026 is the Go idna / net/http hostname validation issue, but the lpm helper only downloads from code-defined hosts. `cmd/populator/modules.go:20` and `cmd/populator/modules.go:25` hardcode the module registry URL, `cmd/populator/Populator.go:23` and `cmd/populator/Populator.go:29` show only the embedded package manifest is iterated, and the HTTP helpers consume those fixed URLs (`cmd/populator/artifactory_maven.go:28`, `cmd/populator/artifactory_maven.go:30`, `cmd/populator/artifactory_github.go:31`, `cmd/populator/artifactory_github.go:32`, `internal/app/utils/Http.go:13`, `internal/app/utils/Http.go:25`). There is no attacker-controlled hostname input path here, so the Punycode hostname-validation bug is unreachable in this deployment.

CVE-2026-46600 / GO-2026-5942 requires the Go cgo DNS resolver and invalid SVCB/HTTPS DNS answers, but the lpm release build disables cgo (`Makefile:21`, `Makefile:22`, `Makefile:36`, and `Makefile:37` set `CGO_ENABLED=0`). The runtime code only creates ordinary HTTP clients and performs fixed-URL downloads (`internal/app/utils/Http.go:13`, `internal/app/utils/Http.go:25`, `cmd/populator/artifactory_maven.go:28`, `cmd/populator/artifactory_maven.go:30`, `cmd/populator/artifactory_github.go:31`, `cmd/populator/artifactory_github.go:32`), so the cgo resolver path used by the advisory is not reachable here.

vulnerabilities.description: Denial-of-service on Windows applications using Netty. Netty attempts to read OS identification files even on Windows systems where they don't natively exist. An attacker with local access can create an oversized (>1GB) file at these paths, causing Netty to load it into memory and exhaust the JVM heap, crashing the application.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Requires pre-existing local attacker write access to root-level filesystem paths.

ratings.justification: Requires an attacker who already has local write access to root-level paths, a precondition beyond Liquibase's threat model for a database migration CLI tool.

analysis.detail: Netty's PlatformDependent unconditionally attempts to read /etc/os-release and /usr/lib/os-release-style paths for OS identification, including on Windows where these paths don't natively exist. Exploitation requires an attacker who already has local filesystem write access sufficient to plant a >1GB file at one of these root-level paths ahead of JVM startup — a precondition that itself requires the host to already be compromised at a level exceeding what this DoS provides. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver; Liquibase does not read or configure these paths itself.

vulnerabilities.description: See CVE-2026-33871 entry on netty-codec-http2. Mirrored for sibling transport artifact.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not run an HTTP/2 server.

ratings.justification: Server-side HTTP/2 vulnerability in a transport-only sibling artifact.

analysis.detail: Scanner over-match: same root assessment as netty-codec-http2 (see above). netty-transport-classes-epoll is the Linux epoll native transport — no HTTP/2 frame decoder. CPE-based scanners propagate the CVE here despite the artifact not containing the vulnerable parser.

vulnerabilities.description: Denial-of-service on Windows applications using Netty via a null-byte-filled file at an OS-identification path, causing an infinite loop during charset decoding instead of the earlier oversized-file crash.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Requires pre-existing local attacker write access to root-level filesystem paths.

ratings.justification: Requires an attacker who already has local write access to root-level paths, a precondition beyond Liquibase's threat model for a database migration CLI tool.

analysis.detail: Incomplete fix to CVE-2024-47535 (see above): a null-byte-filled file at the same Windows os-release-style paths causes InputStreamReader / BufferedReader to loop filling the line buffer with replacement characters without hitting a line break. Same precondition as CVE-2024-47535 — requires an attacker who already has local filesystem write access to plant the malicious file before JVM startup. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver; Liquibase does not read or configure these paths itself.

vulnerabilities.description: Memory leak in Netty's DNS codec when processing malicious DNS response packets containing invalid domain names. The record decoder fails to release allocated ByteBuf resources before the IDNA-validation exception is thrown, allowing incremental memory exhaustion through sustained malicious DNS responses.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Requires a compromised or malicious DNS resolution path, which lies outside Liquibase's outbound-client threat model.

ratings.justification: Requires a compromised or malicious DNS server able to forge responses to Liquibase's own outbound resolution queries.

analysis.detail: Netty's DNS record decoder fails to release allocated ByteBuf resources before throwing on domain names that violate IDNA rules, leaking memory per malformed record. Unlike the server-side Netty DNS codec findings above, this path is reached during Liquibase's own outbound DNS resolution, but only triggers when the DNS server answering that resolution (or an on-path attacker able to forge responses) returns malformed records. This requires a compromised or malicious DNS resolution path — an attacker already in a position to forge DNS responses to Liquibase's outbound queries could achieve more direct impact (e.g. redirecting database connections) than a gradual memory leak. No CVE has been assigned to this advisory at the time of assessment. Netty is a transitive dependency from Azure SDK, Cassandra driver, and MongoDB driver — used only as a client-side transport for outbound connections.

vulnerabilities.description: Little CMS (lcms2) through 2.18 has an integer overflow in CubeSize in cmslut.c because the overflow check is performed after the multiplication.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. The reported package does not exist in the Liquibase Secure image.

ratings.justification: The image does not contain Little CMS at all; the scanner matched an Oracle OpenJDK CPE against a Temurin JRE base image.

analysis.detail: Little CMS 2.18 integer overflow in CubeSize/cmslut.c. The scan reported Oracle OpenJDK 21.0.11+10-LTS, but Liquibase Secure is built from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (core/docker/Dockerfile:1) and contains no Little CMS/lcms2 references in the repository, so the scanner's openjdk match is a false product match.

vulnerabilities.description: Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: Libraries). Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u491, 8u491-perf, 11.0.31, 17.0.19, 21.0.11, 25.0.3, 26.0.1; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.19 and 21.0.11; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.18.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for the Liquibase Secure container. The image uses a Temurin JRE and does not run as an Oracle Java client runtime.

ratings.justification: The assessed image is a Linux CLI container built on Temurin JRE, not an Oracle Java SE/GraalVM client runtime with sandboxed applet or Web Start exposure.

analysis.detail: Oracle Java SE Libraries vulnerability. The scan reported 21.0.11+10-LTS and the dispatch payload lists fixed_version 1.8.0_502, but Liquibase Secure is built from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (core/docker/Dockerfile:1), not an Oracle Java SE or GraalVM client runtime. The container runs the Liquibase CLI through docker-entrypoint.sh rather than a sandboxed Java Web Start or applet environment (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8), so the client runtime required by the advisory is absent.

vulnerabilities.description: Vulnerability in the Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition product of Oracle Java SE (component: Install). Supported versions that are affected are Oracle Java SE: 8u501, 11.0.32, 17.0.20, 21.0.12, 25.0.4, 26.0.2; Oracle GraalVM for JDK: 17.0.20 and 21.0.12; Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition: 21.3.19. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows low privileged attacker with logon to the infrastructure where Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition executes to compromise Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in takeover of Oracle Java SE, Oracle GraalVM for JDK, Oracle GraalVM Enterprise Edition.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for the Liquibase Secure container. The image is built from Temurin's release archive and never invokes Oracle's Java installer.

ratings.justification: CNA (Oracle) score; NVD had not yet published its own score at assessment time.
The vulnerable component (Oracle's Java installer) is not present in the Liquibase Secure image; the container runs a Temurin JRE unpacked from a release archive.

analysis.detail: Oracle Java SE/GraalVM Install-component vulnerability, fixed upstream in 21.0.12 (Oracle August 2026 CPU). The flaw is in Oracle's Java installer, a packaging component that ships only with Oracle's own distribution. Liquibase Secure is built from eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble (core/docker/Dockerfile:1) via docker-entrypoint.sh (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:8); Temurin's JRE is unpacked from a release archive, not installed through Oracle's installer, so the vulnerable component is not present in the image at all. There is no Adoptium/Temurin tracking entry for this CVE. Unlike the other Oracle Java SE entries in this batch (sandbox/Web Start applicability mismatches, justified requires_environment), this is a component absence -- the installer isn't shipped at all -- hence code_not_present.

vulnerabilities.description: Enforce a recursion limit in Unmarshal to prevent stack exhaustion when parsing deeply-nested, recursive structures.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. The vulnerable stdlib path is not exercised by the default Liquibase Secure runtime.

ratings.justification: lpm is only an optional helper and the default container path never feeds attacker-controlled nested data into Go's encoding/json Unmarshal path.

analysis.detail: Go stdlib recursion-limit issue in Unmarshal. The dispatch payload reports go1.26.5 and fixed versions 1.25.13, 1.26.6, and 1.27.0-rc.3. The secure Docker image installs lpm 0.3.6 from a release ZIP (core/docker/Dockerfile:34-50) and the runtime entrypoint only invokes lpm when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4, core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:5). The default Liquibase runtime path executes the Java CLI directly, so the Unmarshal path that would process attacker-controlled deeply nested data is not exercised. This assessment also covers the GO-2026-5972 alias.

vulnerabilities.description: When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads a few bytes from each new connection to see if they contain the HTTP/2 client preface. ReadHeaderTimeout is unexpectedly not being applied when doing this.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not run an HTTP/2 server.

ratings.justification: The vulnerable code path requires a server-side HTTP/2 listener, which Liquibase Secure does not provide.

analysis.detail: Go stdlib HTTP/2 preface timeout issue. The dispatch payload reports go1.26.5 and fixed versions 1.25.13, 1.26.6, and 1.27.0-rc.3. Liquibase Secure is a database migration CLI, not an HTTP server. The secure Docker image installs lpm 0.3.6 from a release ZIP (core/docker/Dockerfile:34-50) and only invokes it when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4, core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:5), so the server-side unencrypted HTTP/2 listener required by the advisory is absent.

vulnerabilities.description: Previously, pathological inputs could close an unescaped '/' early, allowing for attack-controlled data to inject arbitrary content, potentially leading to XSS.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. The affected parser path is not used in this image.

ratings.justification: Liquibase Secure does not render attacker-controlled HTML in the Go runtime path that would expose this slash-parsing behavior.

analysis.detail: Go stdlib unescaped-slash parsing issue. The dispatch payload reports go1.26.5 and fixed versions 1.25.13, 1.26.6, and 1.27.0-rc.3. Liquibase Secure's runtime path is the Java CLI plus the optional lpm helper (core/docker/Dockerfile:34-50 and core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4, core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:5). The container does not parse attacker-controlled HTML/XML content through this stdlib path, so the vulnerable behavior is not exercised.

vulnerabilities.description: Previously, DecodeElement would reset the depth counter causing it to never fire; this could lead to stack exhaustion.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. The vulnerable XML decode path is not used by the default Liquibase Secure runtime.

ratings.justification: The vulnerable stdlib XML decoder is not exercised by Liquibase Secure's default CLI path or its optional lpm helper.

analysis.detail: Go stdlib DecodeElement depth-counter issue. The dispatch payload reports go1.26.5 and fixed versions 1.25.13, 1.26.6, and 1.27.0-rc.3. Liquibase Secure installs lpm 0.3.6 from a release ZIP (core/docker/Dockerfile:34-50) and only invokes it when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4, core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:5), so the XML decode path that would process attacker-controlled nested elements is not reached. This assessment also covers the GO-2026-6088 alias.

vulnerabilities.description: Previously, resolving relative paths containing parent directory ('..') segments performed string conversions and buffer rewrites on each step, resulting in quadratic time complexity and high memory allocation overhead.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. The affected path resolution routine is not used in the default Liquibase Secure runtime.

ratings.justification: Liquibase Secure does not expose an attacker-controlled path resolution surface in the Go stdlib runtime path.

analysis.detail: Go stdlib relative-path resolution quadratic complexity issue. The dispatch payload reports go1.26.5 and fixed versions 1.25.13, 1.26.6, and 1.27.0-rc.3. The secure Docker image only executes the Java CLI by default and invokes lpm 0.3.6 only when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (core/docker/Dockerfile:34-50 and core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4, core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:5). The vulnerable path resolution behavior is not exercised on attacker-controlled input in this deployment.

vulnerabilities.description: See CVE-2026-33870 entry on netty-codec-http. Mirrored for sibling transport artifact so scanners receive the same not_affected statement.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not run an HTTP server.

ratings.justification: Server-side HTTP vulnerability in a transport-only sibling artifact.

analysis.detail: Scanner over-match: same root assessment as netty-codec-http (see above). netty-transport-classes-kqueue provides macOS/BSD kqueue(2) native transport classes — no HTTP parser code. CPE-based propagation only.

vulnerabilities.description: Handshake messages, such as KeyUpdate, are always considered as state-advancing, regardless of whether a handshake has been completed or not. As a result, a malicious client can keep sending KeyUpdate messages to force the server to keep performing key derivation operations indefinitely.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not run a TLS server.

ratings.justification: The vulnerable TLS handshake behavior requires a server endpoint, which Liquibase Secure does not provide.

analysis.detail: Go stdlib KeyUpdate state-advance issue in TLS handshakes. The dispatch payload reports go1.26.5 and fixed versions 1.25.13, 1.26.6, and 1.27.0-rc.3. Liquibase Secure is a database migration CLI, not a TLS server; the secure Docker image installs lpm 0.3.6 from a release ZIP (core/docker/Dockerfile:34-50) and only invokes it when INSTALL_MYSQL is set (core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4, core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:5). The server-side TLS handshake path required by the advisory is absent.

vulnerabilities.description: A malicious GOSUMDB was capable of serving arbitrary module content not contained within the transparency log. This attack allows for a coordinating GOPROXY and GOSUMDB to serve a client malicious module content that cannot be detected by evaluating the transparency log. In order to determine if you have been affected: rm -r go.sum go.work.sum vendor/ && go mod tidy
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not run Go module verification workflows at runtime.

ratings.justification: The vulnerable GOSUMDB / module-verification path is only relevant when Go tooling performs module resolution. Liquibase Secure only ships lpm as an optional helper and does not run go mod or sumdb verification at runtime.

analysis.detail: Go stdlib GOSUMDB transparency-log bypass issue. NVD fixes the Go 1.25 line in 1.25.13 and the 1.26 line in 1.26.6. The scan reported installed version go1.25.1 for the bundled lpm helper. Liquibase Secure installs lpm 0.3.6 from a release ZIP in core/docker/Dockerfile:23, core/docker/Dockerfile:44, core/docker/Dockerfile:49 and only invokes it when INSTALL_MYSQL is set in core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4, core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:5. The default runtime path executes the Java Liquibase CLI directly, and this repository has no go.mod, go.sum, or go mod tidy workflow that would exercise the vulnerable Go module-verification path.

vulnerabilities.description: A malicious GOPROXY was previously capable of forging up to two sumdb tiles that allow for a requested module to bypass the GOSUMDB check and persist attacker-controlled module content to a local Go module cache. This attack allows for a malicious GOPROXY to serve malicious module content that cannot be detected by evaluating the transparency log. All tiles are now correctly verified against their parents. In order to determine if you have been affected: rm -r go.sum go.work.sum vendor/ && go mod tidy
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not run Go module download or cache-verification workflows at runtime.

ratings.justification: The vulnerable GOPROXY / sumdb cache path is only relevant when Go tooling resolves modules. Liquibase Secure only ships lpm as an optional helper and does not run go mod or GOPROXY-driven cache population at runtime.

analysis.detail: Go stdlib GOPROXY sumdb-tile forgery issue. NVD fixes the Go 1.25 line in 1.25.13 and the 1.26 line in 1.26.6. The scan reported installed versions go1.25.3 and go1.25.1 for the bundled lpm helper across the supplied image tags. Liquibase Secure installs lpm 0.3.6 from a release ZIP in core/docker/Dockerfile:23, core/docker/Dockerfile:44, core/docker/Dockerfile:49 and only invokes it when INSTALL_MYSQL is set in core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:4, core/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh:5. The default runtime path executes the Java Liquibase CLI directly, so the Go module-download and cache-population path described by the advisory is not exercised here.

vulnerabilities.description: Improper Access Control, Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Apache Tomcat leads to security constraint bypass if a constraint for a longer path is specified before a more restrictive constraint for a shorter sub-path. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.24, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.57, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.120, from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.109. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.25, 10.1.58, 9.0.121, which fixes the issue.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not start a Tomcat server.

ratings.justification: Security-constraint evaluation only happens inside a running Tomcat servlet container processing deployed web.xml descriptors. Liquibase never starts a Tomcat server or deploys a web.xml, so the vulnerable code path is never exercised.

analysis.detail: Security constraint bypass when a `<security-constraint>` for a longer path is declared before a more restrictive constraint for a shorter sub-path in web.xml. Requires an active Tomcat servlet container evaluating security constraints against deployed web.xml descriptors. Liquibase is a CLI tool that uses picocli for command-line parsing and never starts a Spring application context or Tomcat server (grep across core/, pro/, and all extension modules for `org.apache.catalina.startup.Tomcat`, `new Tomcat(`, `TomcatServletWebServerFactory`, and `@SpringBootApplication` returns zero hits in production source). tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web, pulled in by the Spring Boot integration module for users who embed Liquibase in their own Spring apps. No servlet container is started, so no security-constraint evaluation ever occurs.

vulnerabilities.description: Authentication Bypass by Capture-replay vulnerability in Apache Tomcat's DIGEST authenticator. If, before windowSize requests have been made, a client makes a DIGEST authenticated request with a nonceCount on the upper boundary of the replay window then that request is replayable once only while the associated nonceCount remains within the replay window. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.24, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.57, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.120. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.25, 10.1.58 or 9.0.121, which fix the issue.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not start a Tomcat server.

ratings.justification: DIGEST authentication replay only applies to a running Tomcat servlet container configured with a DIGEST authenticator. Liquibase never starts a Tomcat server and never configures DIGEST authentication, so the vulnerable code path is never exercised.

analysis.detail: Authentication bypass by capture-replay in Tomcat's DIGEST authenticator: a nonceCount on the upper boundary of the replay window can be replayed once before it ages out. Requires an active Tomcat servlet container with DIGEST authentication configured and processing inbound authenticated requests. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Spring application context or Tomcat server (grep across core/, pro/, and all extension modules for `org.apache.catalina.startup.Tomcat`, `new Tomcat(`, `TomcatServletWebServerFactory`, and `@SpringBootApplication` returns zero hits in production source). tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web, pulled in by the Spring Boot integration module for users who embed Liquibase in their own Spring apps. No DIGEST authenticator is ever configured or invoked.

vulnerabilities.description: Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Apache Tomcat's FORM authentication process allows the bypassing of a security constraint that limits user access to a resource via POST but not GET. This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.24, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.57, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.120. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.25, 10.1.58 or 9.0.121, which fixes the issue.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not start a Tomcat server.

ratings.justification: FORM-authentication constraint bypass only applies to a running Tomcat servlet container with FORM authentication and a method-scoped security constraint configured. Liquibase never starts a Tomcat server and never configures FORM authentication, so the vulnerable code path is never exercised.

analysis.detail: Incorrect Authorization in Tomcat's FORM authentication process allows bypassing a security constraint that limits a user to POST access on a resource (not GET). Requires an active Tomcat servlet container with FORM authentication and a POST-only security constraint configured. Liquibase is a CLI tool that never starts a Spring application context or Tomcat server (grep across core/, pro/, and all extension modules for `org.apache.catalina.startup.Tomcat`, `new Tomcat(`, `TomcatServletWebServerFactory`, and `@SpringBootApplication` returns zero hits in production source). tomcat-embed-core is a transitive dependency from spring-boot-starter-web, pulled in by the Spring Boot integration module for users who embed Liquibase in their own Spring apps. No FORM authenticator or security constraint is ever configured.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to 4.1.137.Final and 4.2.17.Final, io.netty.handler.ssl.SslClientHelloHandler#decode checks the wrong offset before reading the four-byte TLS handshake header, so a ClientHello whose handshake header spans records can cause an IndexOutOfBoundsException and invoke select(ctx, null). This selects the default SslContext instead of the SNI-specific context. In deployments where per-SNI clientAuth=REQUIRE is the sole mutual TLS gate, the default SslContext uses clientAuth=NONE or clientAuth=OPTIONAL, and no application-layer certificate verification exists, an unauthenticated remote attacker can bypass the protected route's mutual TLS requirement. This issue is fixed in versions 4.1.137.Final and 4.2.17.Final.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not run a Netty server or configure per-SNI mutual-TLS routing.

ratings.justification: NVD had not published a CVSS vector for this CVE as of the assessment date; GHSA rates overall severity as CRITICAL.

The vulnerable code path only triggers inside a Netty server decoding inbound TLS ClientHello records for SNI-based routing. Liquibase never runs a Netty server; all netty-handler usage in the distribution is transitive, client-side, and outbound only.

analysis.detail: SslClientHelloHandler#decode checks the wrong offset before reading the four-byte TLS handshake header, so a ClientHello whose handshake header spans records can throw IndexOutOfBoundsException and fall back to the default SslContext instead of the SNI-specific one. This only becomes an mTLS bypass in a deployment that (a) runs a Netty server accepting inbound TLS connections, (b) uses per-SNI SslContext selection as the sole mutual-TLS gate (clientAuth=REQUIRE on the SNI context, weaker on the default), and (c) has no application-layer certificate check. Liquibase never runs a Netty server: a grep across all Java sources for ServerBootstrap, NioServerSocketChannel, SniHandler, AbstractSniHandler, and SslClientHelloHandler returns zero hits: netty-handler is present only as a transitive dependency of outbound HTTP/TLS clients (Azure SDK's azure-core-http-netty, the AWS SDK, the Couchbase client, the Cassandra JDBC driver). The scanner found netty-handler below the fixed versions in five bundled jars (Docker Scan run https://github.com/liquibase/liquibase-pro/actions/runs/34365994421): liquibase-commercial-cassandra.jar 4.1.119.Final, liquibase-azure.jar 4.1.135.Final, liquibase-aws-extension.jar 4.1.136.Final, liquibase-commercial-couchbase.jar 4.2.16.Final, and liquibase-azure-deps.jar (unlabeled in the scan, same shaded copy as liquibase-azure.jar); none of them run a Netty server, so the version gap does not matter to this assessment.

vulnerabilities.description: Apache HttpComponents Client, when using the classic (blocking) I/O model, fails to release the underlying connection back to the connection manager if the response contains an invalid or unsupported Content-Encoding header value. Repeated requests to a malicious or misbehaving server leak connections and eventually exhaust the connection pool, producing a denial of service. The async I/O model is not affected. Fixed in version 5.6.3.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Upgrade to the latest Liquibase Secure release when available. The one reachable usage path is additionally protected by only ever talking to a trusted, TLS-authenticated AWS endpoint.

ratings.justification: The dependency is already pinned past the fixed version (httpclient5 5.6.4 >= 5.6.3) across every module that resolves it, and the one reachable classic-client usage path only ever talks to a trusted, TLS-authenticated first-party AWS endpoint, not an attacker-controlled server.

analysis.detail: httpclient5 is already pinned to 5.6.4 (past the 5.6.3 fix), but that alone only holds until a future downgrade, so we also checked reachability of the classic (blocking) client this CVE affects. Two usages exist: a bundled PII-detection filter, which is unreachable - it requires a policy-loading path Liquibase's checks engine never invokes - and the AWS SDK's synchronous Secrets Manager client, which is real but only ever talks to AWS's own TLS-authenticated endpoint. Exploitation needs that server to repeatedly send malformed Content-Encoding responses, so a remote attacker can't trigger this without already controlling or intercepting trusted AWS traffic - the same precondition used for the related Netty HTTP/2 CVEs.

vulnerabilities.description: Git, before versions 2.48.1, 2.47.3, 2.46.5, 2.45.4, and 2.44.3, has a vulnerability where a Git client using a terminal that supports ANSI escape sequences can have those sequences, when written to the sideband channel used by the server to transmit informational or error messages during clone/fetch/push, misrepresent the state of a fetch/pull/push or otherwise mislead the user into executing untrusted scripts.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not invoke git at runtime, and the only git usage (CI checkout of this repo's own trusted remote) is not the exploit scenario this CVE describes.

ratings.justification: Liquibase runtime code never invokes git against an untrusted remote; the only git usage in this repo is CI checkout of its own trusted remote.

analysis.detail: Exploitation requires cloning, fetching from, or pushing to an attacker-controlled Git remote that injects malicious ANSI escape sequences over the sideband channel. Liquibase runtime code never shells out to `git clone`, `git fetch`, or `git push` against any remote — a stronger, structural argument than merely trusting a given remote. A source review confirmed no process/exec invocation of git anywhere in Liquibase's runtime code. The only git usage in this repo at all is CI's own checkout step, which clones this repository's own trusted GitHub remote with a git binary version pinned by the runner image, not by this repo — not the exploit scenario this CVE describes.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. In versions 4.2.0.Final through 4.2.15.Final and 4.1.0.Final through 4.1.135.Final, Bzip2Decoder's run-length encoding (RLE) state machine can enter an infinite loop when processing a malformed bzip2 stream, permanently occupying the event-loop thread at 100% CPU and causing denial of service. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Neither module ever configures or wires bzip2 compression into a Netty pipeline.

ratings.justification: Bzip2Decoder is never reachable in either module assessed here - Cassandra's native protocol supports only LZ4/Snappy compression and configures none, and Azure's Netty HTTP client never wires a Bzip2Decoder into any pipeline.

analysis.detail: netty-codec resolves below the 4.1.136.Final fix line for both modules assessed here (4.1.130.Final for liquibase-commercial-cassandra via cassandra-jdbc-wrapper -> java-driver-core, 4.1.135.Final for liquibase-azure via azure-core-http-netty). The vulnerable class, Bzip2Decoder, is never reachable in either: the Cassandra native protocol's compression negotiation supports only LZ4/Snappy and this extension doesn't configure compression at all, while Azure's Netty HTTP client never wires a Bzip2Decoder into any pipeline (Azure HTTP responses use gzip/deflate/br, and a class-listing search of the Azure SDK jars for Bzip-related symbols returns zero hits).

vulnerabilities.description: See CVE-2026-33871 entry on netty-codec-http2. Mirrored for sibling transport artifact.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not run an HTTP/2 server.

ratings.justification: Server-side HTTP/2 vulnerability in a transport-only sibling artifact.

analysis.detail: Scanner over-match: same root assessment as netty-codec-http2 (see above). netty-transport-classes-kqueue is the macOS/BSD kqueue native transport — no HTTP/2 frame decoder. CPE-based propagation only.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. In versions 4.2.0.Final through 4.2.15.Final and 4.1.0.Final through 4.1.135.Final, the SpdyHttpDecoder handler in Netty's SPDY-to-HTTP codec allocates a pooled ByteBuf when processing a client-initiated SYN_STREAM frame and stores the partially constructed FullHttpRequest in messageMap; when the remote peer sends RST_STREAM for that stream, or the accumulated content exceeds maxContentLength, the decoder removes the entry without releasing the pooled ByteBuf, leading to native memory exhaustion. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Neither module ever wires an SPDY codec into any pipeline.

ratings.justification: The vulnerable code is Netty's legacy SPDY-to-HTTP codec, which neither module's HTTP client ever negotiates or wires in, regardless of Netty version. Cassandra's copy is additionally already past the fixed version as defense-in-depth.

analysis.detail: The real vulnerable code is Netty's legacy SPDY-to-HTTP codec (SpdyHttpDecoder), not generic HTTP/2 handling — confirmed against the GitHub Security Advisory. Neither liquibase-commercial-cassandra's AWS SDK secretsmanager -> netty-nio-client chain nor liquibase-azure's azure-core-http-netty ever negotiates or wires an SPDY codec; both only ever speak HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2, so SpdyHttpDecoder is never reached by either. Cassandra's copy of netty-codec-http also already resolves at 4.1.137.Final via the AWS SDK chain, past the 4.1.136.Final fix line, as secondary defense-in-depth; Azure's copy remains on the vulnerable 4.1.135.Final and relies solely on the SPDY-never-used argument.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. In versions 4.2.0.Final through 4.2.15.Final and 4.1.0.Final through 4.1.135.Final, a remote unauthenticated peer can leak one direct ByteBuf per HTTP/2 DATA frame in applications that enable HTTP/2 content decompression via DelegatingDecompressorFrameListener: when a DATA frame is processed for a stream whose decompressor has already been closed, the retained buffer is not released on the error path, eventually exhausting direct memory and crashing the JVM. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required under normal deployment (both modules only connect to trusted, TLS-authenticated first-party endpoints — AWS Secrets Manager and Microsoft Azure services respectively).

ratings.justification: Both modules' HTTP/2 clients only ever connect to a single trusted, TLS-authenticated first-party endpoint (AWS Secrets Manager for Cassandra, Microsoft Azure services for Azure), so exploiting the leak requires one of those trusted endpoints to misbehave or be compromised.

analysis.detail: netty-codec-http2's DelegatingDecompressorFrameListener DATA-frame handling is exercised by both modules' outbound HTTP/2 clients: liquibase-commercial-cassandra's AWS SDK secretsmanager -> netty-nio-client chain, and liquibase-azure's azure-core-http-netty. Exploiting the leak requires a malicious or misbehaving HTTP/2 peer; both modules only ever connect to a single trusted, TLS-authenticated first-party endpoint (AWS Secrets Manager for Cassandra, Microsoft Azure services for Azure), so the same "requires a malicious peer, and we only talk to a trusted endpoint" argument applies to both. Cassandra's copy also happens to already resolve at 4.1.137.Final, past the 4.1.136.Final fix line, as secondary defense-in-depth; Azure's copy remains on the vulnerable 4.1.135.Final and relies solely on the trusted-endpoint argument.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final, SpdyFrameCodec continues driving the zlib inflater on a SPDY header block even after the raw header data exceeds maxHeaderSize and the frame is marked truncated, so CPU work and heap allocations continue for the full compressed payload - a decompression-bomb pattern applied to a protocol-level control channel. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Neither module ever wires an SPDY codec into any pipeline.

ratings.justification: Neither module's outbound HTTP client ever negotiates or wires an SPDY codec - both only ever speak HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 - so SpdyFrameCodec's zlib header decompression is never reached.

analysis.detail: SPDY is a legacy protocol that neither module's outbound HTTP client ever negotiates or wires a codec for, regardless of Netty version: liquibase-commercial-cassandra's AWS SDK secretsmanager -> netty-nio-client chain and liquibase-azure's azure-core-http-netty both only ever speak HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2, never SPDY, so SpdyFrameCodec's zlib header decompression is never reached by either. Cassandra's copy of netty-codec-http also already resolves at 4.1.137.Final, past the 4.1.136.Final fix line, as secondary defense-in-depth.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final, Netty's SPDY SETTINGS decoder accepts a peer-declared SETTINGS entry count up to the 24-bit frame-length limit and materializes every unique setting ID in DefaultSpdySettingsFrame's backing TreeMap without a count budget, allowing a remote SPDY/3.1 peer to send a roughly 2 MiB SETTINGS frame that creates 262,144 map entries and amplifies network input into heap growth. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Neither module ever wires an SPDY codec into any pipeline.

ratings.justification: Neither module's outbound HTTP client ever negotiates or wires an SPDY codec - both only ever speak HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 - so DefaultSpdySettingsFrame's SPDY SETTINGS decoder is never reached.

analysis.detail: SPDY is a legacy protocol that neither module's outbound HTTP client ever negotiates or wires a codec for, regardless of Netty version: liquibase-commercial-cassandra's AWS SDK secretsmanager -> netty-nio-client chain and liquibase-azure's azure-core-http-netty both only ever speak HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2, never SPDY, so DefaultSpdySettingsFrame's SPDY SETTINGS decoder is never reached by either. Cassandra's copy of netty-codec-http also already resolves at 4.1.137.Final, past the 4.1.136.Final fix line, as secondary defense-in-depth.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final, Netty's HTTP/2-to-HTTP/1.x translation layer (Http2StreamFrameToHttpObjectCodec / InboundHttp2ToHttpAdapter) fails to deduplicate or validate Host headers when an HTTP/2 client supplies both the :authority pseudo-header and a literal host header in a single HEADERS frame, producing an HttpRequest with two differing Host headers that can be used to bypass request-routing logic. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Neither module performs HTTP/2-to-HTTP/1.x protocol translation.

ratings.justification: This CVE concerns HTTP/2-to-HTTP/1.x translation performed by a front-end server or proxy; both modules are pure outbound HTTP/2 clients and never perform protocol translation.

analysis.detail: This CVE concerns the HTTP/2-to-HTTP/1.x translation layer a front-end server or proxy uses (e.g. InboundHttp2ToHttpAdapter) to receive and translate inbound HTTP/2 requests — a server/proxy-side concept neither module ever exercises, both being pure outbound HTTP/2 clients: liquibase-commercial-cassandra's AWS SDK secretsmanager -> netty-nio-client chain and liquibase-azure's azure-core-http-netty each only ever act as a direct HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 client, never a protocol-translating front end. Cassandra's copy of netty-codec-http2 also already resolves at 4.1.137.Final, past the 4.1.136.Final fix line, as secondary defense-in-depth.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final, HttpContentEncoder maintains a per-channel acceptEncodingQueue that accumulates attacker-controlled data without a size limit; the queue is filled on the I/O thread for every inbound HTTP request and drained only when the application writes a non-1xx response, allowing an attacker to exploit HTTP/1.1 pipelining to exhaust resources. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Neither module runs an HTTP server that would use HttpContentEncoder.

ratings.justification: HttpContentEncoder encodes outbound responses on the server side of an HTTP exchange; neither module ever runs an HTTP server, only makes outbound client requests.

analysis.detail: HttpContentEncoder encodes outbound responses on the server side of an HTTP exchange, a role neither module ever plays: liquibase-commercial-cassandra's AWS SDK secretsmanager -> netty-nio-client chain and liquibase-azure's azure-core-http-netty each only make outbound client requests and decode inbound responses, never run an HTTP server. Cassandra's copy of netty-codec-http also already resolves at 4.1.137.Final, past the 4.1.136.Final fix line, as secondary defense-in-depth.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Versions 4.2.0.Final through 4.2.15.Final and 4.1.0.Final through 4.1.135.Final are affected by a logical-operator error in CorsHandler's origin evaluation that allows the shortCircuit() security control to be bypassed entirely by sending a request with an Origin: null header, forwarding unauthorized cross-origin requests to the backend application. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Neither module runs an HTTP server that would use CorsHandler.

ratings.justification: CORS enforcement is inherently server-side and neither module ever runs an HTTP server, so CorsHandler is never reached by either.

analysis.detail: CORS enforcement is inherently server-side, and neither module ever runs an HTTP server: liquibase-commercial-cassandra's AWS SDK secretsmanager -> netty-nio-client chain and liquibase-azure's azure-core-http-netty both only ever make outbound client requests, so CorsHandler is never reached by either. Cassandra's copy of netty-codec-http also already resolves at 4.1.137.Final, past the 4.1.136.Final fix line, as secondary defense-in-depth.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final, the newHandshakeResponse methods of WebSocketServerHandshaker07 and WebSocketServerHandshaker08 complete a WebSocket protocol upgrade based solely on the presence of a Sec-WebSocket-Version: 7 (or 8) header, without verifying the mandatory Connection: Upgrade and Upgrade: websocket headers, enabling HTTP request smuggling / protocol-confusion attacks through intermediaries that don't recognize the request as an Upgrade. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Neither module runs a WebSocket server.

ratings.justification: WebSocketServerHandshaker07/08 are server-side handshake classes and neither module ever runs a WebSocket server, only makes plain HTTPS client calls.

analysis.detail: WebSocketServerHandshaker07/08 are server-side handshake classes, and neither module ever runs a WebSocket server: liquibase-commercial-cassandra's AWS SDK secretsmanager -> netty-nio-client chain and liquibase-azure's azure-core-http-netty each only make plain HTTPS client calls, never WebSocket connections. Cassandra's copy of netty-codec-http also already resolves at 4.1.137.Final, past the 4.1.136.Final fix line, as secondary defense-in-depth.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final, io.netty.handler.codec.dns.AbstractDnsRecord, io.netty.handler.codec.dns.DefaultDnsRecordDecoder.decodeRecord(), and io.netty.handler.codec.dns.DnsCodecUtil.decompressDomainName() failed to release retained or newly allocated ByteBuf objects when IDN.toASCII() or encodeDomainName() rejected a malformed domain name, allowing unauthenticated remote DNS packets to leak direct memory incrementally until denial of service. Fixed in 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Risk-accepted pending an upstream reactor-netty/Netty release with the fix. This assessment assumes the deployment's DNS resolution path is not exposed to an attacker with network-level access (e.g. internal/corporate DNS resolvers, not an open or adversarial network) - confirm this assumption holds for how this module is actually deployed before treating this as closed. Revisit once reactor-netty ships a release with netty-resolver-dns >= 4.1.136.Final.

ratings.justification: Exploitation requires network-level access to the deployment's resolver path, not a plain remote attacker - the resolved hostname is always operator-configured (never changelog-derived), narrowing but not eliminating the attack surface pending an upstream fix.

analysis.detail: netty-resolver-dns:4.1.135.Final (below the 4.1.136.Final fix line) resolves for this module via reactor-netty-http:1.2.18 -> reactor-netty-core:1.2.18, and unlike the other Netty CVEs assessed here, is genuinely wired into every outbound connection by default via reactor-netty-core's NameResolverProvider — this is not a code-not-reachable case. The hostname resolved is always operator-supplied configuration, never derived from changelog content: Key Vault modifiers parse the vault host from a Liquibase configuration value, and Blob Storage access uses a separately configured storage-account property, so an attacker can't inject a resolution target purely via a malicious changelog. That only rules out attacker-chosen domains, though — it doesn't rule out this CVE's actual mechanism, a malformed DNS response to an otherwise-legitimate query. DNS isn't TLS-authenticated the way this module's HTTP/2 traffic is, so the "trusted endpoint" argument used for the HTTP/2 CVEs on this module doesn't transfer here. Exploitation requires network-level access to the deployment's DNS resolution path — an assumption about the deployment environment this codebase can't verify. No newer reactor-netty release exists yet with a fixed Netty.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty is a network application framework for development of protocol servers and clients. Prior to versions 4.1.135.Final and 4.2.15.Final, before reading the first request-line, HttpObjectDecoder skips every byte for which Character.isISOControl(b) is true (0x00–0x1F and 0x7F) as well as all whitespace. RFC 9112 §2.2 only asks servers to ignore empty CRLF lines preceding the request-line. Silently absorbing other control characters can be exploited for request-boundary confusion where a front-end component treats those bytes differently.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not run a Netty HTTP server, and the shipped netty-codec-http version is already newer than the fixed 4.1.135.Final release.

ratings.justification: The vulnerable logic is in Netty's server-side HTTP request parser; Liquibase ships only outbound client usage of this dependency and no Liquibase source wires Netty HTTP server handlers.

analysis.detail: Fixed in netty-codec-http 4.1.135.Final; this repository's current build already resolves netty-codec-http 4.1.136.Final via the Azure extension's Netty HTTP client, past the fix line. NVD ties this CVE to HttpObjectDecoder's server-side request-line parsing. Liquibase is never deployed as an HTTP backend behind a proxy or otherwise runs a Netty HTTP server, and a source review found no code wiring HttpObjectDecoder, HttpServerCodec, ServerBootstrap, CorsHandler, or HttpContentEncoder — the vulnerable parser path is not reachable regardless of version.

Go stdlib vulnerability in the Docker base image. Liquibase is a Java application and does not execute Go code at runtime. The Go binary is part of Docker base image tooling and is not invoked by Liquibase.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to 4.2.13.Final and 4.1.133.Final, Netty's chunk size parser silently overflows int, enabling request smuggling attacks.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not run a Netty HTTP server, and the shipped netty-codec-http version is already newer than the fixed 4.1.133.Final release.

ratings.justification: The affected parser is only relevant when Netty is decoding inbound HTTP requests on the server side; Liquibase does not expose that path.

analysis.detail: Fixed in netty-codec-http 4.1.133.Final; this repository's current build already resolves netty-codec-http 4.1.136.Final via the Azure extension's Netty HTTP client, past the fix line. NVD describes a chunk-size integer overflow in Netty's HttpObjectDecoder — a server-side request-smuggling issue. Liquibase never runs a Netty HTTP server, and a source review found no code wiring HttpObjectDecoder, HttpServerCodec, ServerBootstrap, CorsHandler, or HttpContentEncoder — the vulnerable parser path is not reachable regardless of version.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty allows request-line validation to be bypassed when a DefaultHttpRequest or DefaultFullHttpRequest is created first and its URI is later changed via setUri(). If attacker-controlled input reaches setUri(), HttpRequestEncoder and RtspEncoder can write CRLF sequences into the request line, enabling HTTP request smuggling or RTSP request injection.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required under normal deployment. Liquibase connection URIs are operator-configured, and the shipped netty-codec-http version is already newer than the fixed 4.1.133.Final release.

ratings.justification: Exploitation depends on attacker-controlled URIs reaching Netty's outbound request builder, but Liquibase endpoint configuration is administrator-supplied rather than untrusted user input.

analysis.detail: Fixed in netty-codec-http 4.1.133.Final; this repository's current build already resolves netty-codec-http 4.1.136.Final via the Azure extension's Netty HTTP client, past the fix line. This CVE requires attacker-controlled data to reach DefaultHttpRequest.setUri() before Netty emits an outbound request line. Liquibase's connection URIs are operator-configured, not supplied by untrusted end-users, and a source review found no code calling DefaultHttpRequest, DefaultFullHttpRequest, setUri(), HttpRequestEncoder, or RtspEncoder directly.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty is a network application framework for development of protocol servers and clients. Prior to versions 4.1.135.Final and 4.2.15.Final, netty_unix_socket_recvFd can leak file descriptors when a peer sends an SCM_RIGHTS control message carrying two descriptors. The issue is reachable via Epoll/KQueue DomainSocketChannel when the application opts into DomainSocketReadMode.FILE_DESCRIPTORS.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not use Netty domain sockets or FILE_DESCRIPTORS mode, and the shipped epoll artifact is already at the fixed 4.1.135.Final release.

ratings.justification: The vulnerable path depends on Netty domain-socket file-descriptor passing, which Liquibase does not configure or reference in source.

analysis.detail: Fixed in netty-transport-native-epoll 4.1.135.Final; this repository's current build already resolves that exact version via the Azure extension's Netty HTTP client. NVD states the leak is only reachable through Epoll/KQueue DomainSocketChannel when an application opts into the non-default DomainSocketReadMode.FILE_DESCRIPTORS mode. A source review found no code referencing DomainSocket, DomainSocketChannel, DomainSocketReadMode, EpollDomainSocket, KQueueDomainSocket, recvFd, or SCM_RIGHTS — Liquibase does not use the domain-socket feature the vulnerability requires, regardless of version.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty is a network application framework for development of protocol servers and clients. Prior to versions 4.1.135.Final and 4.2.15.Final, Netty's DNS resolver uses a predictable PRNG for generating DNS transaction IDs and defaults to a static UDP source port, reducing query entropy and enabling DNS cache poisoning.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Upgrade to the latest Liquibase Secure release when available — this fix is present in this development branch but hasn't shipped yet. This is a real, reachable dependency (not a never-used feature), so the version fix is the actual protection here, not a defense-in-depth extra.

ratings.justification: The shipped dependency is already at the fixed 4.1.135.Final release, eliminating the vulnerable PRNG/default-port implementation from the delivered artifact.

analysis.detail: Fixed in netty-resolver-dns 4.1.135.Final; this repository's current build already resolves that exact version via the Azure extension's Netty stack. Unlike most other Netty CVEs assessed for this module, netty-resolver-dns is not a "never used" case — it is genuinely wired into every outbound connection by default via reactor-netty's DNS resolution path (see the CVE-2026-73508 assessment on this same subcomponent for the detailed reachability analysis), so the decisive protection here is the version fix, not a reachability argument.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to 4.2.13.Final and 4.1.133.Final, HttpObjectDecoder strips a conflicting Content-Length header for HTTP/1.1 chunked requests but not for HTTP/1.0, enabling request smuggling when a downstream component trusts Content-Length over Transfer-Encoding.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not run a Netty HTTP server, and the shipped netty-codec-http version is already newer than the fixed 4.1.133.Final release.

ratings.justification: The affected logic is only relevant when Netty decodes inbound HTTP/1.0 requests on the server side; Liquibase does not expose that path.

analysis.detail: Fixed in netty-codec-http 4.1.133.Final; this repository's current build already resolves netty-codec-http 4.1.136.Final via the Azure extension's Netty HTTP client, past the fix line. NVD ties this flaw to HttpObjectDecoder's handling of inbound HTTP/1.0 requests carrying both Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length — a server-side request-smuggling issue. Liquibase never runs a Netty HTTP server, and a source review found no code wiring HttpObjectDecoder, HttpServerCodec, ServerBootstrap, CorsHandler, or HttpContentEncoder — the vulnerable parser path is not reachable regardless of version.

vulnerabilities.description: Connect2id Nimbus JOSE + JWT 10.0.x before 10.0.2 and 9.37.x before 9.37.4 allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service via a deeply nested JSON object supplied in a JWT claim set, because of uncontrolled recursion. Fixed in 9.37.4 and 10.0.2.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. This repository does not depend on nimbus-jose-jwt in any resolved build.

ratings.justification: The flagged package is not present in this repository's resolved dependency tree under any module — the scanner matched a transitive test-scope dependency that never reaches a downstream consumer's classpath.

analysis.detail: A scanner flagged com.nimbusds:nimbus-jose-jwt@10.0.1 as reachable through the com.azure:azure-identity dependency chain used by the Azure extension. Resolving the actual dependency tree shows azure-identity 1.18.4 pulls com.microsoft.azure:msal4j 1.23.1, and msal4j's only reference to com.nimbusds (oauth2-oidc-sdk, which itself depends on nimbus-jose-jwt) is declared with test scope in msal4j's own POM — a test-scope dependency does not propagate to a downstream consumer's compile/runtime classpath. Resolving the dependency tree for io.netty and com.nimbusds artifacts across every module that pulls azure-identity or msal4j transitively (the Azure extension, and the Databricks and MongoDB commercial extensions, which carry defensive ProGuard keep/dontwarn rules referencing com.nimbusds left over from an earlier dependency configuration) confirms zero resolved com.nimbusds:nimbus-jose-jwt artifacts anywhere in this repository's build. The scanner's finding does not correspond to an actual dependency in this codebase.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty is an asynchronous event-driven network application framework. In netty-codec-compression versions 4.1.124.Final and below, and netty-codec versions 4.2.4.Final and below, specially crafted input can cause BrotliDecoder and certain other decompression decoders to allocate a large number of reachable byte buffers, leading to denial of service. Fixed in 4.1.125.Final of netty-codec and 4.2.5.Final of netty-codec-compression.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase does not invoke BrotliDecoder or accept untrusted compressed Netty payloads.

ratings.justification: Liquibase does not configure or call Netty's Brotli decompression handlers, so the vulnerable decoder path is not reachable even before considering that the resolved netty-codec version is already above the fixed release.

analysis.detail: Fixed in netty-codec 4.1.125.Final / netty-codec-compression 4.2.5.Final; this repository's current build already resolves netty-codec 4.1.136.Final via the Azure and Cassandra extensions' Netty dependency chains, past the fix line. Liquibase does not accept compressed HTTP payloads from untrusted clients, and a source review found no code referencing BrotliDecoder, BrotliEncoder, BrotliOptions, or io.netty.handler.codec.compression.Brotli — the vulnerable decompression path is not exercised, regardless of version.

vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in p11-kit. The RPC message attribute parsing functions form a mutually-recursive call chain with no recursion depth limit when processing nested CKA_WRAP_TEMPLATE, CKA_UNWRAP_TEMPLATE, and CKA_DERIVE_TEMPLATE attributes. An unauthenticated attacker with local access to the p11-kit RPC Unix domain socket can send a specially crafted request with deeply nested template attributes, causing stack exhaustion and crashing the p11-kit server process and its dependent services.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for the stock Liquibase Secure container. If a derived image adds and exposes a p11-kit RPC service, update the base package to a fixed build first.

ratings.justification: Exploitation requires a running p11-kit RPC service and its Unix domain socket. The stock Liquibase Secure container only starts the Liquibase CLI and does not configure or launch p11-kit at runtime.

analysis.detail: The reported package is inherited from the container base image. Exploitation requires a running p11-kit RPC Unix domain socket and local access to that service. Liquibase Secure does not start p11-kit or any auxiliary daemon: the container entrypoint only execs the Liquibase CLI, and a source review of the Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts found no reference to p11-kit or pkcs11. Without a p11-kit RPC service/socket in the deployed container, the required runtime environment is absent.

vulnerabilities.description: A timing-based side-channel flaw was found in libgcrypt's RSA implementation that may allow a remote attacker to initiate a Bleichenbacher-style attack, which can lead to the decryption of RSA ciphertexts.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase's Java runtime does not use libgcrypt; the package is present only as a transitive dependency of unrelated OS tooling this container never invokes.

ratings.justification: The JVM does not link or call libgcrypt; the package is pulled in only by unrelated GnuPG/apt/systemd tooling this container never invokes, and the base image already ships the fixed version.

analysis.detail: A timing side-channel in libgcrypt's RSA implementation could enable a Bleichenbacher-style decryption attack (the "Marvin Attack"). The container base image currently ships libgcrypt20 1.10.3-2ubuntu0.2, the fixed release (confirmed by pulling the current base image and checking installed package versions directly, since this OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the base image resolves to at build time). Independent of the version, checking the Java runtime's own library linkage shows it does not link libgcrypt at all; the package is pulled in only as a dependency of GnuPG/apt/systemd tooling (gpg, gpgv, gpg-agent, dirmngr, libapt-pkg, libsystemd0), none of which Liquibase invokes. Java uses its own JCE crypto providers, not system libgcrypt.

vulnerabilities.description: IO::Uncompress::Unzip versions before 2.215 for Perl propagate an uncaught exception when parsing a zip header with a malformed DOS date. The _dosToUnixTime() function calls Time::Local::timelocal() without an eval guard; a header whose date field decodes to an out-of-range month, day, or hour causes the exception to propagate out of the caller, which expects undef plus an error variable instead.

vulnerabilities.description: A flaw was found in the libblkid library of util-linux. During nested partition probing, the BSD, Minix, Solaris x86, and UnixWare partition probers cache a raw pointer to a parent partition entry in a dynamically allocated array; when subsequent partition additions reallocate the array, the pointer becomes stale, leading to a heap use-after-free read. An attacker who can present a crafted block device image can trigger this without user interaction, since libblkid is invoked automatically by udev/udisks as root on block-device hot-plug events.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required for the stock Liquibase Secure container, which runs no block-device hot-plug management daemon.

ratings.justification: Exploitation requires udev/udisks probing a crafted block device on a hot-plug event; the stock container runs no such daemon and performs no block-device management.

analysis.detail: This use-after-free in libblkid's nested partition probing (BSD, Minix, Solaris x86, UnixWare probers) is triggered automatically by udev/udisks as root on a block-device hot-plug event, such as a USB insertion or a loop-mounted disk image — containers do not perform hot-plug block-device management, and a source review of the Dockerfiles and entrypoint scripts found no invocation of udev, udisks, blkid, or any partition-probing tool; the stock container's entrypoint execs only the Liquibase CLI. vulnerabilities.description: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final, HttpPostRequestEncoder constructs multipart HTTP request bodies by directly concatenating user-supplied filenames and field names into Content-Disposition MIME headers without validating or sanitizing CRLF characters. Since MIME headers are delimited by CRLF, an attacker who controls the filename can inject arbitrary MIME headers into the multipart body part. Fixed in versions 4.1.136.Final and 4.2.16.Final.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure's multipart upload implementation uses the AWS SDK's REST-level multipart API, not Netty's multipart encoder classes.

ratings.justification: The vulnerable path depends on Netty's multipart request encoder and attacker-controlled filenames reaching it, but this repository never references those classes and its own multipart logic uses the AWS SDK's REST-level API instead.

analysis.detail: Fixed in netty-codec-http 4.1.136.Final per NVD and GHSA. This repository's current build already resolves netty-codec-http 4.1.136.Final via the Azure extension's Netty HTTP client, past the fix line. This CVE is specific to Netty's HttpPostRequestEncoder multipart body construction from attacker-controlled filenames and field names, but this repository's only multipart upload implementation (S3 object uploads in the AWS extension) uses the AWS SDK's REST-level multipart API (separate part-numbered PUT requests), not Netty's multipart/form-data encoder — a fundamentally different mechanism. A source review found no references to HttpPostRequestEncoder, DiskFileUpload, MemoryFileUpload, or MixedFileUpload anywhere in this repository, so the vulnerable encoder path is not reachable regardless of version.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to 4.1.137.Final and 4.2.17.Final, io.netty.handler.codec.http.cors.CorsHandler's setVaryHeader method replaces application-defined Vary headers (such as Authorization or Cookie) with Origin. This allows a caching proxy or CDN sitting in front of a server using CorsHandler to reuse one user's authenticated response for another user, disclosing sensitive information. Fixed in versions 4.1.137.Final and 4.2.17.Final.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. This repository never runs an HTTP server or uses CorsHandler; all netty-codec-http usage is transitive and client-side.

ratings.justification: CorsHandler only affects servers that add CORS response headers. This repository never runs an HTTP server; all netty-codec-http usage is transitive and client-side only.

analysis.detail: CorsHandler applies CORS response headers on the server side of an HTTP exchange; this repository never runs an HTTP server that uses it. A source review found no references to CorsHandler or CorsConfig anywhere in this repository's own code; every module that bundles netty-codec-http does so only as a transitive dependency of an outbound HTTP client (the AWS SDK's netty-nio-client, the Azure SDK's azure-core-http-netty, the Couchbase Java client, and the Cassandra driver's own AWS SDK chain), never as a server. The AWS extension and the Cassandra extension already resolve netty-codec-http at 4.1.137.Final, past the fix line, as defense-in-depth; the Azure extension remains on the vulnerable 4.1.135.Final and the Couchbase client's shaded copy remains on 4.2.16.Final, both relying solely on the reachability argument.

vulnerabilities.description: Netty is an asynchronous, event-driven network application framework. Prior to 4.1.137.Final and 4.2.17.Final, the default SniHandler constructors use pre-handshake ClientHello aggregation implemented in SslClientHelloHandler, which repeatedly recopies all previously received bytes each time it processes another fragment of a ClientHello split across TLS records. An unauthenticated attacker can advertise a large ClientHello and deliver it in thousands of tiny records, causing quadratic CPU consumption on the event loop and degrading TLS handling for other clients. Fixed in versions 4.1.137.Final and 4.2.17.Final.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. This repository never runs a Netty server or configures per-SNI TLS routing.

ratings.justification: The vulnerable code path only triggers inside a Netty server aggregating inbound TLS ClientHello records for SNI-based routing. This repository never runs a Netty server; all netty-handler usage is transitive, client-side, and outbound only.

analysis.detail: This CVE affects the same pre-handshake ClientHello aggregation code in SslClientHelloHandler as CVE-2026-75595, already assessed in this file: a server-side SNI-routing feature that repeatedly recopies buffered bytes while reassembling a fragmented ClientHello, causing quadratic CPU consumption when an attacker splits a large ClientHello across many small TLS records. This only matters to a deployment running a Netty server with per-SNI SslContext selection (SniHandler/AbstractSniHandler). A source review found no references to ServerBootstrap, NioServerSocketChannel, SniHandler, AbstractSniHandler, or SslClientHelloHandler anywhere in this repository; netty-handler is present only as a transitive dependency of outbound HTTP/TLS clients (the AWS SDK's netty-nio-client, the Azure SDK's azure-core-http-netty, the Couchbase Java client, and the Cassandra driver's own AWS SDK chain), none of which run a Netty server. The AWS extension already resolves netty-handler at 4.1.137.Final, past the fix line, as defense-in-depth; the Azure extension remains on 4.1.135.Final, the Cassandra extension on 4.1.130.Final, and the Couchbase client's shaded copy on 4.2.16.Final, all relying solely on the reachability argument.

As secondary defense-in-depth, this CVE affects Netty's server-side HTTP chunk-size parser; a source review found no references to HttpObjectDecoder, HttpServerCodec, ServerBootstrap, or NioServerSocketChannel anywhere in this repository, so the vulnerable server-side parser path would not be reachable even independent of version.

vulnerabilities.description: GNU Tar through 1.35 allows file overwrite via directory traversal in crafted TAR archives, with a certain two-step process. First, the victim must extract an archive that contains a ../ symlink to a critical directory. Second, the victim must extract an archive that contains a critical file, specified via a relative pathname that begins with the symlink name and ends with that critical file's name. Here, the extraction follows the symlink and overwrites the critical file. This bypasses the protection mechanism of "Member name contains '..'" that would occur for a single TAR archive that attempted to specify the critical file via a ../ approach. For example, the first archive can contain "x -> ../../../../../home/victim/.ssh" and the second archive can contain x/authorized_keys. This can affect server applications that automatically extract any number of user-supplied TAR archives, and were relying on the blocking of traversal. This can also affect software installation processes in which "tar xf" is run more than once.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure only uses tar once at image build time on its own verified release artifact and never on attacker-supplied runtime input.

ratings.justification: Exploitation requires repeated extraction of attacker-supplied TAR archives; Liquibase Secure uses tar only once during image build on a verified release archive and never at container runtime.

analysis.detail: The scanned image reports tar 1.35+dfsg-3build1, below Ubuntu's fixed 1.35+dfsg-3ubuntu0.2, but this issue requires extracting attacker-supplied TAR archives more than once into the same directory. Liquibase Secure invokes GNU tar exactly once during image build to unpack its own SHA-256-verified release archive and does not invoke tar at container runtime.

vulnerabilities.description: The infocmp command-line tool in ncurses before 6.5-20251213 has a stack-based buffer overflow in analyze_string in progs/infocmp.c.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not invoke the infocmp utility or process untrusted terminfo data in its stock runtime path.

ratings.justification: The vulnerable path is in the infocmp utility, which the Liquibase Secure build and stock runtime do not invoke.

analysis.detail: The scanned image reports libncursesw6 6.4+20240113-1ubuntu2, below Ubuntu's fixed 6.4+20240113-1ubuntu2.1, but this issue is in ncurses' infocmp utility. The stock Liquibase Secure image runs the Liquibase CLI non-interactively, and a review of its build and runtime path found no invocation of infocmp or processing of attacker-supplied termcap or terminfo input.

vulnerabilities.description: A use-after-free vulnerability exists in libcurl when an application configures an HTTP/2 stream-dependency tree via CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS or CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS_E, subsequently invokes curl_easy_reset(), and finally terminates the handle with curl_easy_cleanup(). During this final cleanup phase, libcurl attempts to access and modify an internal structure that was already freed during the reset operation.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure does not call curl or the vulnerable libcurl stream-dependency APIs in its stock build or runtime path.

ratings.justification: The vulnerable behavior requires specific libcurl API calls that are absent from Liquibase Secure's build and runtime path.

analysis.detail: The scanned image reports curl 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.10, below Ubuntu's fixed 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.11, but this issue affects applications that configure libcurl stream dependencies and then reset and clean up the same handle. Liquibase Secure's build path uses wget for downloads, not curl, and a review of the secure-image build and stock runtime path found no use of curl or the affected libcurl APIs.

vulnerabilities.description: An integer underflow vulnerability was found in MIT krb5 in the berval2tl_data() function in plugins/kdb/ldap/libkdb_ldap/ ldap_principal2.c. The function performs an unsigned subtraction (bv_len - 2) without a prior bounds check. When bv_len is 0 or 1, the subtraction wraps to a large value which is then truncated to uint16_t. The subsequent malloc succeeds and memcpy reads up to 65534 bytes from a 0-1 byte buffer, resulting in a heap out-of-bounds read. The attack vector involves a malicious or compromised LDAP KDB backend returning a krbExtraData attribute with bv_len < 2, triggering the underflow when the KDC or kadmind reads principal data.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. The stock Liquibase Secure image is not deployed as a Kerberos KDC or kadmind with an LDAP KDB backend.

ratings.justification: Exploitation requires a Kerberos KDC or kadmind using the LDAP KDB backend, which is not part of the Liquibase Secure deployment model.

analysis.detail: The scanned image reports libgssapi-krb5-2 1.20.1-6ubuntu2.6, below Ubuntu's fixed 1.20.1-6ubuntu2.7, but this integer-underflow flaw is in MIT krb5's LDAP KDB backend when a KDC or kadmind reads malformed krbExtraData from a malicious or compromised LDAP backend. Liquibase Secure ships the package only as part of the inherited base image and runs the Liquibase CLI, not a Kerberos KDC or kadmind with an LDAP KDB backend.

vulnerabilities.description: GNU Wget does not validate the IP address provided by an FTP PASV response while operating in FTP passive mode. A malicious FTP server, or an HTTP server that redirects to an FTP URL, can exploit this behavior to redirect Wget's data connection to an arbitrary IP address and port. This allows an attacker to forge server-side requests from the machine running Wget, potentially accessing localhost services or internal network resources.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. Liquibase Secure uses wget only for fixed HTTPS downloads during image build and not in its runtime path.

ratings.justification: The vulnerable behavior requires Wget FTP passive-mode transfers, while Liquibase Secure uses wget only for fixed HTTPS downloads at image build time and not at runtime.

analysis.detail: The scanned image reports wget 1.21.4-1ubuntu4.1, below Ubuntu's fixed 1.21.4-1ubuntu4.4, but this issue requires Wget to follow an attacker-controlled FTP passive-mode data connection. Liquibase Secure uses wget only during image build to fetch its release tarball and the lpm zip over HTTPS, and it does not invoke wget at container runtime.

vulnerabilities.description: The iconv() function in the GNU C Library versions 2.43 and earlier may crash due to an assertion failure when converting inputs from the IBM1390 or IBM1399 character sets, which may be used to remotely crash an application.
